title: Avlat
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great sage among the nations, Shmuel’s friend and companion. [Avodah Zarah 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.30a.5) relates that they sat together when cooked wine was brought. Avlat drew back his hand to avoid touching it, but Shmuel told him that cooked wine was not subject to the prohibition of libation wine. In [Shabbat 129a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.129a.19) Avlat calls Shmuel “the sage of the Jews.” In [Shabbat 156b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.156b.2-3), as they sat watching men go to the marsh, Avlat said: “That man will not return: a snake will bite and kill him.” Shmuel replied, “If he is an Israelite, he will go and return,” and so he did. In [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.3.3.13) and [Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.2.5.4), Avlat questions Levi the eunuch; Hyman says that without doubt it should read Levi bar Sisi.[^1]

notes.text: The two Jerusalem Talmud passages name Levi Sarisa and use a eunuch in the ensuing analogy. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=198&lang=en) also records Avlat asking Levi. Hyman is certain the name should instead be Levi bar Sisi.
